concepts.name: Machine Learning
concepts.definition: Machine learning is a field of AI where computers learn patterns from data instead of following hand-written rules. A model is trained on examples and then makes predictions on new data.

concepts.name: Deep Learning
concepts.definition: Deep learning is a branch of machine learning that uses neural networks with many layers. It works well on images, audio, and text because it can learn complex features on its own.

concepts.name: Natural Language Processing
concepts.definition: Natural language processing is the area of AI concerned with understanding and generating human language. It covers tasks such as translation, summarizing, and answering questions.

concepts.name: Computer Vision
concepts.definition: Computer vision is the area of AI that enables computers to interpret images and video. Applications include face unlocking, medical image analysis, and self-driving car perception.

concepts.name: Neural Network
concepts.definition: A neural network is a model made of connected layers of simple units that pass numbers forward and adjust their connection strengths during training. It is the basic building block of deep learning.

resources.title: But what is a neural network? (3Blue1Brown video)

concepts.name: Transformer
concepts.definition: A transformer is a neural network design that processes all parts of an input at once using attention. Most modern large language models are built on this architecture.

resources.title: Attention Is All You Need (original paper)

concepts.name: Attention
concepts.definition: Attention is a mechanism that lets a model weigh which parts of its input matter most for each output. In language, it helps a word take meaning from the other words around it.

concepts.name: Diffusion Model
concepts.definition: A diffusion model creates images by learning to reverse a process that gradually adds noise to images. Generating starts from random noise and removes it step by step until a picture appears.

concepts.name: Large Language Model
concepts.definition: A large language model is an AI system trained on very large amounts of text to predict and generate language. It powers chatbots and many writing and coding tools.

concepts.name: Multimodal Model
concepts.definition: A multimodal model can work with more than one type of data, such as text, images, and audio. It can, for example, answer questions about a photo you upload.

concepts.name: Open-Source Model
concepts.definition: An open-source or open-weight model is an AI model whose trained parameters are publicly released so anyone can download, run, or modify it, subject to its license.

concepts.name: Token
concepts.definition: A token is a small piece of text, often a word or part of a word, that a language model reads and writes one at a time. Usage limits and costs are often measured in tokens.

concepts.name: Context Window
concepts.definition: The context window is the maximum amount of text, measured in tokens, that a language model can consider at one time. Information outside the window is not visible to the model.

concepts.name: Embedding
concepts.definition: An embedding turns a piece of text, an image, or other data into a list of numbers that captures its meaning. Items with similar meanings get similar numbers, which makes search by meaning possible.

concepts.name: Vector Database
concepts.definition: A vector database stores embeddings and finds the ones closest in meaning to a query quickly. It is a common storage layer for retrieval-based AI applications.

concepts.name: RAG
concepts.definition: Retrieval-Augmented Generation is a method where a system first searches a set of documents for relevant text and gives it to a language model. The model then answers using that material, which helps with accuracy and recent information.

concepts.name: Training
concepts.definition: Training is the process of adjusting a model's parameters using data so its predictions improve. It is the expensive step that comes before a model is used.

resources.title: Linear regression: Loss (Google ML Crash Course)

concepts.name: Inference
concepts.definition: Inference is using a trained model to produce an output, such as an answer or a prediction, for new input. It is what happens each time you send a message to a chatbot.

concepts.name: Supervised Learning
concepts.definition: Supervised learning trains a model on examples that come with correct answers, such as photos labeled with what they show. The model learns to predict the label for new examples.

concepts.name: Reinforcement Learning
concepts.definition: Reinforcement learning trains an agent by rewarding good actions and penalizing bad ones through trial and error. It is used in game-playing AI and to help align language models with human preferences.

concepts.name: Fine-Tuning
concepts.definition: Fine-tuning continues training an existing model on a smaller, specific dataset so it performs better for a particular task or style. It is cheaper than training a model from scratch.

concepts.name: LoRA
concepts.definition: LoRA is a fine-tuning method that trains a small set of added parameters instead of changing the whole model. This makes customizing large models much less costly in memory and compute.

resources.title: LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models (paper)

concepts.name: Prompt Engineering
concepts.definition: Prompt engineering is the practice of writing clear instructions, examples, and context so a language model gives better answers. It requires no changes to the model itself.

concepts.name: Hallucination
concepts.definition: A hallucination is when an AI model produces information that sounds confident but is false or made up. It is a known limitation of language models, so answers should be checked for important facts.

resources.title: Survey of Hallucination in Natural Language Generation (paper)

concepts.name: Guardrails
concepts.definition: Guardrails are rules, filters, and checks placed around an AI system to limit harmful, off-topic, or unsafe outputs. They can run before a request reaches the model or after it responds.

concepts.name: Benchmark
concepts.definition: A benchmark is a standard set of tests used to compare AI models on tasks such as reasoning, coding, or language understanding. Scores help people compare models, though they do not capture everything.

concepts.name: AI Agent
concepts.definition: An AI agent is a system that uses a language model to pursue a goal across several steps. It can plan, call tools, check results, and adjust its approach without a person directing every step.

concepts.name: Tool Use
concepts.definition: Tool use lets a language model request actions such as searching the web, running code, or reading a calendar. The system runs the action and returns the result to the model.

concepts.name: Model Context Protocol
concepts.definition: The Model Context Protocol is an open standard that lets AI applications connect to outside tools and data sources in a consistent way. A single MCP server can serve many different AI clients.

concepts.name: Chatbot
concepts.definition: A chatbot is a program that holds a conversation in natural language. Modern chatbots are usually built on large language models.
